title: Generosity Is a Default Setting
why_read: A practical, data-driven investigation into USB tethering speed issues with a concrete diagnostic tool and real measurements across many phones.
analysis: The author built tether-report, a Linux tool that diagnoses why USB tethering runs slower than the phone's radio without consuming cellular data, based on 40 measurements across 14 phones, and found a default setting change that improved throughput from 15 to 106 Mbps. This is a legitimately useful, measurement-backed networking troubleshooting piece with a concrete artifact (open-source tool) behind it, wrapped in unnecessary charity-framing narrative. Worth reading for anyone doing mobile tethering or Linux networking diagnostics work.
